title: marketplace-launch-storyboard-and-copy-snippets
content:
Purpose
---
Working draft: combine a short launch storyboard, prioritized asset checklist, copy snippets for listing variants, and minimal compliance/ops acceptance criteria. Goal: give PM/Design/Legal a single place to grab copy and do quick QA before we hand assets to partner marketplaces (AWS, Azure, GCP).

High-level launch narrative (storyboard)
---
1) Teaser to partner channel owners (D-14): 1-paragraph announcement + hero screenshot. Ask for pre-approval and expected go-live window.
2) Asset drop (D-7): supply final hero image, 1-min demo MP4, 3 screenshot variants, SKU manifest, and short/long descriptions.
3) Listing goes live (D0): coordinate with channel ops, confirm billing mapping, verify telemetry events and install metrics feed.
4) Post-launch (D+7): check engagement metrics, request placement/feature if thresholds met.

Headline / short pitch (variants)
---
Variant A (concise, product-led): "Redwood Inference — predictable, production-ready LLM inference across hosted, dedicated and private deployments."
Variant B (value-first, ops): "Scale LLM inference with low-latency routing, cost controls, and SLA-backed capacity."
Variant C (developer hook): "Ship LLM features faster — consistent API, built-in caching, and one runtime for hosted or private deployments."

One-line strap copy (for hero/summary)
---
- "High-performance, cost-aware LLM inference — cloud-hosted or in your VPC."
- "Turnkey inference with observability, rollouts and predictable economics."

Long description (800–1,000 chars)
---
Redwood Inference is a developer-first platform that makes running LLMs in production predictable and economical. Use a single API to generate text, chat, and embeddings while retaining control over latency, cost, and data locality. Choose hosted inference for rapid time-to-value, reserved Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput, or Private deployments for regulated workloads. Redwood's runtime optimizes for batching, KV cache reuse, and quantization-aware execution, while the Console gives per-route cost/latency visibility, rollout controls, and automatic fallbacks to keep applications online.

Key bullets (store as 3–5 quick wins to use in bullets on marketplace pages)
---
- Multi-mode: hosted, reserved dedicated pools, and VPC/on-prem private deployments.
- Cost levers: intelligent batching, prefix caching, and quantization profiles.
- Reliability: SLA-backed Dedicated capacity + automated fallbacks.
- Developer UX: simple REST/SDK, streaming, function calling, and model catalog.
- Observability: per-token cost breakdowns, model-level dashboards, and regression alerts.

Required assets (priority order)
---
1) Hero image: 1920x1080, PNG and JPG variants, transparent background optional. (Owner: Design)
2) 1-minute product demo MP4 (mp4, H264, <=50MB). (Owner: Growth)
3) Three screenshots: Console overview, Rollouts dashboard, Runtime performance trace (min 1200x800). (Owner: PM/Design)
4) Short description (<=400 chars) + long description (<=1,000 chars). (Owner: PM)
5) SKU manifest: sku_id, sku_name, unit_of_measure, price_brackets (monthly/annual). (Owner: Revenue Ops)
6) Compliance checklist: SOC2 status statement, data residency options, KMS integrations. (Owner: Security)
7) Legal copy: privacy/data processing addendum pointer and contact. (Owner: Legal)
8) Integration guide (PDF): API keys, sample curl/SDK usage, region mapping, and rollback procedures. (Owner: DevX)

Marketplace-specific notes
---
- AWS: require architecture diagram with VPC flow and IAM example (minimal). Also include a 5-step quickstart for an EC2-hosted private deployment.
- Azure: include AAD SSO instructions and marketplace SKU mapping for reserved capacity.
- GCP: highlight regional presence + notes on GCP billing export integration.

Acceptance criteria (ops QA)
---
- Asset integrity: images and video load without errors on mobile and desktop.
- Copy length: adhere to each marketplace's character limits (tested with sample payload).
- Billing: SKU IDs match internal revenue ops mapping and test invoice shows correct price band.
- Telemetry: listing link includes UTM params; telemetry pipeline receives first 50 impressions within 24 hours.
- Legal: PDPA/GDPR statement present and DPA link accessible.

Launch checklist (actionables with owners)
---
- [ ] Finalize hero + screenshots (Design)
- [ ] Record 1-min demo + optimize size (Growth)
- [ ] Confirm SKU manifest & pricing (Revenue Ops)
- [ ] Legal sign-off on DPA text (Legal)
- [ ] Security sign-off (SOC2/region/cert) (Security)
- [ ] Create marketplace tile + set publish date in partner portal (Partnerships)
- [ ] Run internal QA passes (PM, DevX)
- [ ] Coordinate go/no-go sync 48 hours prior to planned publish (All stakeholders)

Quick creative copy snippets for A/B tests
---
A/B snippet group 1: Cost-focused
- A: "Reduce token costs with smart batching and prefix caching."
- B: "Lower inference bills without sacrificing latency."

A/B snippet group 2: Reliability-focused
- A: "SLA-backed Dedicated pools and automatic fallback to keep apps online."
- B: "Graceful degradation: fallbacks, region routing, and cached prefixes."

Edge-case QA notes (things we've had trouble with before)
---
- Thumbnail rendering differences between partner portals (PNG vs JPG color profile). Export both.
- Video autoplay blocked in some regions; ensure poster frame set correctly.
- Billing SKU rounding: some marketplaces round differently; verify test invoices end-to-end.
- Character-limit truncation: double-check unicode ellipses and long model names in bullet lists.

Open questions / decisions to make
---
- Do we include a partner-specific 30-day trial credit? (Cost / Partnerships decision)
- Which support contact do we expose for private deployments (partner-owned or Redwood-owned escalation)?
- Should we publish a short-case-study mock (1–2 paragraphs + metrics) on launch, or wait for first-customer data?

Notes to reviewers
---
- This is intentionally compact — if Legal or Security want fuller PDP/DPA text, link to Confluence-4521 (linked above).
- If we choose trial credits, Revenue Ops needs 1 week lead time to map promo codes to SKUs.
- Slack threads: #gtm-marketplace (for day-of coordination), #security-compliance for sign-off questions.

Revision history (short)
---
- 2024-11-12: initial draft (Aisha)
- 2024-11-20: added SKU manifest template + AWS notes (Diego)
